name: Progressive Delivery: Blue-Green, Canary Deployments & Feature Toggles
tagline: Decoupling code deployment from feature release via instant Blue-Green cutovers, SLO-gated Canary shifts, and runtime Feature Toggles.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of progressive delivery—from why big-bang deploys cause company-wide outages to automated Canary SLO rollbacks and Expand-Contract DB compatibility.

spark.summary: Progressive delivery decouples code deployment from feature release using Blue-Green instant cutovers, SLO-gated Canary traffic shifting (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), and runtime Feature Toggles on a single trunk.
spark.keyTakeaway: Pair backward-compatible expand-contract DB migrations with automated Canary SLO rollbacks and Feature Toggles so bad releases impact < 1% of traffic and revert in seconds.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **Progressive delivery** separates *deploying a binary* from *exposing a feature to 100% of users* using three complementary mechanisms: **Blue-Green** (two identical environments with an instant load-balancer cutover).

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Automated SLO-Gated Canary Progression & Rollback (CANARY 1% -> 10% -> PROMOTE 50% -> 100% -> AUTO ROLLBACK); Argo Rollouts + Envoy + Prometheus Auto-Rollback (Argo Rollouts -> Envoy Ingress -> Canary v2 (5%) -> Prometheus).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Each deployment strategy trades compute overhead against rollback speed and mixed-version exposure. Argo Rollouts shifts 5% of Envoy ingress traffic to the v2 canary pods, waits 10 minutes, and runs an `AnalysisRun` comparing canary vs. baseline p99 latency and 5xx rate.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore zero-downtime canary rollbacks, unbiased canary evaluation, and DB compatibility.

learningJourney.title: What is Progressive Delivery
learningJourney.explanation: **Progressive delivery** separates *deploying a binary* from *exposing a feature to 100% of users* using three complementary mechanisms: **Blue-Green** (two identical environments with an instant load-balancer cutover), **Canary** (incremental traffic shifting `1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%` gated by automated P99 latency and 5xx SLO checks over 5–15 minute bake windows), and **Feature Toggles** (runtime flags decoupling trunk merges from user cohort activation).

sectionDiagram.title: Automated SLO-Gated Canary Progression & Rollback
sectionDiagram.summary: Automated metric gates halt and revert bad releases before more than a tiny fraction of users are affected.

learningJourney.title: Why we need Progressive Delivery (Bounding Blast Radius)
learningJourney.explanation: Big-bang weekend deploys turn minor regressions—like a memory leak or subtle N+1 query—into company-wide outages requiring frantic hotfixes. By shifting only 1% of traffic to the canary or flipping a feature flag off in <1 second, teams contain blast radius automatically and decouple marketing launches from code pushes.

ideas.title: Expand-Contract DB Compatibility Is Mandatory
ideas.description: During Blue-Green or Canary rollouts, old (v1) and new (v2) replicas share the same database concurrently—never drop or rename columns until v1 pods are 100% drained.

ideas.title: Flag Hygiene Prevents Combinatorial Tech Debt
ideas.description: Assign a 30-day TTL to release toggles and delete stale flags once 100% rolled out.

costs: Requires mature observability, statistical baseline comparison, and automated rollback triggers.

learningJourney.title: How Argo Rollouts Canary Gates are configured
learningJourney.explanation: Use a progressive delivery controller (Argo Rollouts or Flagger) with explicit traffic steps, bake pauses, and an `AnalysisTemplate` querying Prometheus for error rate and p99 latency against the baseline.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```yaml
# Argo Rollouts Canary spec with automated SLO analysis
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
spec:
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
        - setWeight: 5
        - pause: { duration: 10m }
        - analysis:
            templates: [{ templateName: slo-5xx-p99-gate }]
        - setWeight: 25
        - pause: { duration: 10m }
        - setWeight: 100
```

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Blue-Green vs. Canary vs. Rolling Update
learningJourney.explanation: Each deployment strategy trades compute overhead against rollback speed and mixed-version exposure.

benefits: Instant atomic rollback; clean version separation (never mixes v1 and v2 traffic).
costs: Requires 2x peak compute capacity during cutover windows.

benefits: Minimal extra capacity and automated <1–5% blast radius containment.
costs: v1 and v2 run concurrently, requiring backward-compatible APIs and schemas.

benefits: Built-in with zero extra controllers or service mesh.
costs: Lacks automated Prometheus SLO rollback gates—readiness probes alone miss business-logic 500s.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production example: Envoy Weighted Canary + Prometheus Gate
learningJourney.explanation: Argo Rollouts shifts 5% of Envoy ingress traffic to the v2 canary pods, waits 10 minutes, and runs an `AnalysisRun` comparing canary vs. baseline p99 latency and 5xx rate. When canary 5xx spikes above threshold, Argo automatically resets weight to 0% in seconds.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why must database schema changes use the Expand-and-Contract pattern before a Canary or Blue-Green deployment?

options.text: Because v1 and v2 application replicas run concurrently against the same database, so both schemas must remain compatible during rollout and rollback
options.feedback: Correct: dropping or renaming a column used by v1 breaks live traffic and prevents safe rollback.

options.text: Because Envoy proxies cannot route traffic while a PostgreSQL index exists
options.feedback: Envoy routes HTTP/gRPC independently of DB indexes; the constraint is v1/v2 schema compatibility.

options.text: Because Feature Toggles require two separate PostgreSQL clusters
options.feedback: Feature toggles work against a single shared database.
